newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares fell on Wednesday for the second straight day and analysts said the higher turnover and mixed session after price-fixing signalled a fall on Thursday.

But they said many stocks were falling in profit-taking after recent gains and that the overall market could soon rebound, buoyed by the news that the U.S. Federal Reserve did not raise interest rates on Tuesday.

"In the next few days the market should positively react to that decision...with rises today on other European bourses suggesting that we're not threatened with a deeper correction," said Wojciech Bialek, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.2 percent to 14,490.6 points and turnover rose 13.7 percent to 125.1 million zlotys ($45) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 66 to five with seven stocks stable.

Large-cap stocks such as paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw, construction and trading company Mostostal Export and bank BRE, which fell 4.8, 3.7 and 3.1 percent, were seen hit by profit-taking after recent rises, along with top gainer drug maker Jelfa, down 5.3 percent.
Analysts said investors would watch Friday's food-price figure for the second 10 days in September to help determine if inflation would be low enough for an interest-rate cut.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.6 million zlotys ($0.6 million) with biggest mover trader Universal down 5.1 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.1 percent in continuous trade and rose 1.8 percent to 141.5 zlotys ($50.9) in 58.4- million-zloty ($21 million) turnover in the regular bourse session.
Some analysts said the units, reaching a record high in record turnover, could soon hit a correction with capital transferring to stocks.
